newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss lawyers to co-operate in MGAM review.
newsitem.headline: Swiss lawyers to co-operate in MGAM review.

text.p: Two Swiss lawyers who were board members of Luxembourg-based holding companies linked to sacked Deutsche Morgan Grenfell fund manager Peter Young said on Monday they were aiding a company probe into potential irregularites.

"Wyler & Wolf, a law firm in Zurich, has agreed to fully cooperate with the representatives of Morgan Grenfell investigating the difficulties which have arisen in three funds managed by Morgan Grenfell," the firm said in a brief statement.
The firm denied it had "supported" any operations in the case, but did not elaborate and said it would provide no further information.

A public relations specialist hired by the firm said lawyers Juerg Wyler and Marco Wolf had acted as board members for some of the companies in Luxembourg, but he stressed they worked as trustees and did not play an active role in operations.
They are no longer members of the board, he said.
"The role of Wyler & Wolf was very much limited," the spokesman said, adding: "The firm is cooperating fully with Morgan Grenfell and Deutsche Bank."
He declined to comment on media reports that the lawyers had turned over documents detailing trading records at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) funds in question.
MGAM has said it sacked Young for "gross miscounduct". Young, 38, has said he was a scapegoat.

Trading in the MGAM funds was temporarily suspended earlier this month but resumed after a 180 million pound cash injection by Germany's Deutsche Bank. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is the London fund management arm of Deutsche Bank.
